byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: The 2011 census counted 1.21 billion people, three in four of whom could read, and three in five Indians held a mobile phone subscription.

items.title: Population
items.summary: India's population was about 1.24 billion in 2010; the census of 2011 counted 1,210,854,977.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Population, total

items.title: Life expectancy at birth
items.summary: A newborn in 2010 could expect to live about 67 years.

items.title: Who could read
items.summary: At the 2011 census 74 percent of people could read and write, 82 percent of men and 65 percent of women.

items.title: Town and village
items.summary: The 2011 census found 31.16 percent of Indians living in towns and cities and 68.84 percent in rural areas.

items.title: Online
items.summary: About 7.5 percent of Indians used the internet in 2010.

items.title: Mobile phones
items.summary: There were about 60 mobile subscriptions for every 100 people, up from 7.8 in 2005.

foodAndKitchen.standfirst: Zomato, which began as Foodiebay in 2008, took that name in 2010 and listed restaurants with menus online.

items.summary: Pizza chains promised home delivery in 30 minutes.

items.title: Street food

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up
schoolAndChildhood.standfirst: The Right to Education Act came into force on 1 April.

items.title: Right to Education
items.summary: The Right to Education Act came into force on 1 April 2010, making schooling for ages 6 to 14 a legal right.

items.title: Grades in class 10
items.summary: CBSE introduced grading and continuous evaluation for class 10 around 2009-10.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Central Board of Secondary Education

items.title: Tuition
items.summary: Private tuition and coaching classes grew along with school.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: The Delhi Metro's Violet Line opened.

items.title: The Violet Line
items.summary: The Violet Line of the Delhi Metro opened on 3 October 2010.

items.title: A crash at Mangalore
items.summary: On 22 May 2010 an Air India Express flight from Dubai overran the runway at Mangalore's table-top airport and burned, killing 158 of the 166 on board; the inquiry blamed the captain's failure to abort an unstabilised approach.

sensitivity.note: This item describes an air crash that killed 158 people.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: Phones could now move money, and a government demanded access to a smartphone's mail.

items.title: Money by mobile
items.summary: The Immediate Payment Service, letting money move between bank accounts by mobile, was launched on 22 November 2010 with four banks.

items.title: The BlackBerry deadline
items.summary: On 12 August 2010 India gave BlackBerry until 31 August to provide access to its services to the authorities.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: The IPL's third season, played in March and April, was streamed live on YouTube; a kabaddi world cup ended with India beating Pakistan.

items.title: The IPL final
items.summary: Chennai Super Kings beat Mumbai Indians by 22 runs at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai to win the 2010 Indian Premier League, played between 12 March and 25 April.

items.title: Live on YouTube
items.summary: In 2010 the IPL became the first sporting event broadcast live on YouTube.

items.title: Indian Idol
items.summary: Sreeram Chandra won Indian Idol Season 5 on 15 August 2010.

spotlight.title: Recharge culture and the first smartphones
spotlight.standfirst: By 2010 six in ten Indians had a mobile subscription, mostly prepaid and mostly for calls and text, with a smartphone still out of most hands.

items.title: The Nokia era
items.summary: Nokia handsets were the best-known phones in India, with Micromax and others selling cheap dual-SIM models.

items.title: Per-second billing
items.summary: Tata DoCoMo introduced per-second billing in 2009, pushing other firms to cut rates.

items.title: 3G auction
items.summary: The government auctioned 3G spectrum in 2010 and the first 3G services began later that year.

items.title: Keeping your number
items.summary: Mobile number portability began in 2011 and let users change operators.

items.title: Recharge culture
items.summary: Most users bought prepaid top-ups from the corner shop in small amounts.
